Starting in Heilbronn, Germany, G.L.A.S.S aims to transform traditional glass recycling containers into intelligent, connected infrastructure using the G.L.A.S.S box.
G.L.A.S.S uses compact IoT sensor device: G.L.A.S.S uses compact IoT sensor devices equipped with infrared optical sensors to monitor how full public glass recycling containers are.
These sensors collect fill-level informa: These sensors collect fill-level information, which can then be used to provide valuable insights to both municipal waste management services and the public.
Instead of relying entirely on fixed col: Instead of relying entirely on fixed collection schedules, waste management teams can make informed decisions based on actual container capacity.
Less unnecessary driving. More efficient: Less unnecessary driving. More efficient collections. A cleaner city.
By monitoring container fill levels, G.L: By monitoring container fill levels, G.L.A.S.S aims to help municipal waste management services:
Prioritize containers that actually need: Prioritize containers that actually need emptying, reducing unnecessary trips.
Lower fuel consumption and vehicle emiss: Lower fuel consumption and vehicle emissions through more efficient collection planning.
Identify containers approaching capacity: Identify containers approaching capacity before they become a problem.
Analyze usage patterns to help city plan: Analyze usage patterns to help city planners determine where additional recycling containers may be needed.
Use real-time information to improve lon: Use real-time information to improve long-term waste management strategies.
